question.text: The velocity-time relation of an object traveling along a straight path is represented in the given plot. Initially, at time t = 0, the object is situated at a distance of 10 m from the reference mean position. Determine the following:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: The acceleration of the object at the time instants t = 1 s, t = 3 s, and t = 9 s.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: The location of the object relative to the reference mean position at t = 10 s.

parts.label: c
parts.asks:
The displacement-time (s-t) expressions for the periods:
(i) 0 ≤ t ≤ 2 s
(ii) 4 s ≤ t ≤ 8 s

conditions: initial displacement from mean position at t = 0 is 10 m

figure.description: A graph of velocity v (in m/s) on the vertical axis against time t (in s) on the horizontal axis. The curve begins at (0 s, 0 m/s), increases uniformly to (2 s, 10 m/s), remains constant at 10 m/s until t = 4 s, decreases linearly passing through (6 s, 0 m/s) to reach (8 s, −10 m/s), and finally increases linearly to end at (10 s, 0 m/s).

solution.approach: Read acceleration from the slope of each v-t segment, and get position by adding the signed area under v-t to the given starting position.

steps.text: Find the slope of the v-t line at t = 1 s, 3 s and 9 s from the segment each falls in.
steps.equation: a(1 s) = 5 m/s² (0–2 s segment), a(3 s) = 0 (2–4 s segment, constant v), a(9 s) = 5 m/s² (8–10 s segment)

steps.text: Start the position at s = 10 m at t = 0 and add the area under v-t up to each breakpoint to find s at t = 10 s.
For 0 ≤ t ≤ 2 s, v = 5t; integrate to get s(t).
For 4 s ≤ t ≤ 8 s, v = 10 − 5(t − 4), starting from s(4) = 40 m; integrate and collect terms in t.

common_mistakes.text: Reading the acceleration at t = 3 s as nonzero, forgetting that a straight horizontal segment of the v-t graph means zero acceleration.
Writing the s-t equation for 4 s ≤ t ≤ 8 s starting the position from zero instead of from s(4) = 40 m, the value already reached by that time.
